rejected.statement: Energosuchus is an extinct genus of rauisuchian reptile whose name means "active crocodile" in Greek.
rejected.quote: Energosuchus (meaning "active crocodile" in Greek) is an extinct genus of rauisuchian.

rejected.statement: Fossils of Energosuchus have been found along the banks of the Bolshaya Synya river in the Timan-North Urals region of northern European Russia.
rejected.quote: Fossils are present from the upper Karyomayol and lower Synya Formations outcropping along the banks of the Bolshaya Synya river in the Timan-North Urals region in northern European Russia

rejected.statement: Fossils of Energosuchus are also found in the Bukobay Formation in the southern Urals region of Bashkortostan, European Russia.
rejected.quote: as well as from the Bukobay Formation in the southern part of Bashkortostan in the southern Urals of European Russia.

rejected.statement: The fossils of Energosuchus date to the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic.
rejected.quote: Both localities date back to the Ladinian stage of the Middle Triassic.

rejected.statement: Energosuchus is classified within the clade Crurotarsi, the order Rauisuchia, and the family Rauisuchidae.
The type species of the genus Energosuchus is E. garjainovi, described by Ochev in 1986.
Energosuchus lived between 241.464 and 237 million years ago during the Ladinian stage.
rejected.quote: Time range: Ladinian to Ladinian (241.464 to 237 million years ago)

rejected.statement: There are currently two recorded fossil occurrences of Energosuchus in the Paleobiology Database.
